expected_behavior: An in-progress panel drag must be released (dragging set to false / no further pointermove deltas applied) when the tab is backgrounded (visibilitychange with hidden:true). A visibilitychange event reporting hidden:false (foregrounding) must NOT itself cancel or otherwise affect an in-progress drag that started after foregrounding. Ordinary drag start/move/release via pointerdown/pointermove/pointerup must continue to work exactly as before.
allowed_repairs: in the visibilitychange handler, when e.hidden is true, set state.dragging = false (and any equivalent release/cancel of the in-progress gesture)
a broader 'release on interruption' helper invoked from the visibilitychange handler that has the same net effect
forbidden_repairs: ignoring all pointermove events after any visibilitychange has ever fired (over-broad; breaks a fresh drag started after foregrounding)

releasing the drag on every visibilitychange regardless of e.hidden (breaks nothing functionally observable here but is not the targeted fix -- flagged only if it also breaks the foregrounding-does-not-cancel assertion, which a same-tick spurious release would)
removing pointermove handling from panel entirely
